text:
## 설계 (코드 전에 적는다)

**편집기가 먼저, 안 폼은 편집기가 없을 때만.** 사용자 요청이 "vi 나 nano 가 있으면 거기로" 다. 둘을 고르는 키나 설정은 두지 않는다 — 설정으로 가르면 둘째 어휘다(hudg 원칙). 고르는 차례: `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → PATH 의 `vi` → `nano`. 빈 값(빈칸뿐)은 없는 것으로 친다.
- **git 의 `core.editor` 는 안 본다.** git 을 제대로 따르려면 `GIT_EDITOR`·`core.editor` 가 `VISUAL` 보다 **앞**이어야 해서, 반만 따르면 git 과 moai 가 다른 편집기를 띄우는 까닭이 설명 안 된다. 여는 순간 `git` 한 번을 더 부르는 값도 든다. 필요해지면 idea 로 연다.
- 편집기는 **띄울 때 한 번 고른다**(`cmd/tui.rs` 가 환경·PATH 를 읽어 `App::editor` 에 넣는다). App 은 환경을 모른다 — 시험이 세운 App 은 편집기가 없어 오늘처럼 안 폼을 연다.
- `$VISUAL`·`$EDITOR` 는 PATH 에서 찾지 않고 믿는다(git 과 같다). 없는 명령이면 셸이 127 로 끝나고 "담지 않았다" 로 말한다.

**순수한 곳: `src/tui/jotfile.rs` (조각, 순수성 가드 밑).** 환경·파일·프로세스를 모른다.
- `template(into)` — 첫 줄 빈 줄 + `#` 안내(담을 곳의 이름·경로는 `text::one_line`).
- `parse(text) -> Option<(title, body)>` — CRLF·CR 을 줄바꿈으로, **`#` 뒤가 빈칸이거나 줄 끝인 줄만** 주석으로 걷는다(`# 안내`·`#`). `## 설계`·`#tag` 는 본문으로 남는다 — 생각의 본문에 마크다운 제목(`##`)이 흔한데 git 처럼 `#` 로 시작하는 줄을 다 걷으면 말없이 사라진다. 대가는 본문의 `# h1` 이 걷히는 것이고, 안내 주석이 그것을 댄다("본문의 제목은 `##` 부터"). 앞 빈 줄을 건너 첫 줄(앞뒤 빈칸 뗌)이 제목, 그 뒤 앞 빈 줄을 떼고 끝 빈칸을 뗀 것이 본문. 제목이 비면 `None` — git 의 "빈 메시지는 그만둔다" 와 같다.
- `pick(visual, editor, found)` — 고르는 차례. `found` 는 부르는 쪽이 준다.
- `argv(editor, file)` — `sh -c '<editor> "$@"' <editor> <file>`. **파일 경로는 따옴표로 싸지 않고 위치 인자로 넘긴다**(git 의 `launch_editor` 와 같다) — 경로에 빈칸·따옴표가 들어도 셸이 다시 쪼개지 않는다. 편집기 문자열은 셸 규칙으로 쪼갠다(`code --wait`).

**루프가 내리고 올린다, App 은 요청만 세운다.** `n` → `App::open_form` 이 담을 곳을 박은 뒤(moai-fccv 그대로) 편집기가 있으면 `App::edit = Some(Edit { into, text: template })` 를 세운다. 루프(`cmd/tui.rs`)가 사건 하나를 넘긴 뒤 그것을 꺼내 **bracketed paste 끄기 → `ratatui::restore`(raw mode·대체 화면) → 편집기 기다리기 → raw mode·대체 화면·paste 켜기 → `term.clear()`** 를 하고, 결과(`Result<글, 까닭>`)를 `App::edited(into, 결과)` 로 넘긴다. App 은 터미널을 끝까지 모른다.
- 편집기가 도는 동안 **루프 스레드가 `wait` 에 서 있어** 그리기·스피너·`follow` 가 전부 멈춘다. 다시 읽기 스레드는 계속 짓지만 그리지 않는다(그리는 것은 루프 하나다) — 돌아오면 다음 걸음이 받는다.
- **담는 길은 폼과 한 길이다.** `edited` 는 받은 제목·본문으로 `Mode::Idea(Form { into, … })` 를 세우고 `save_idea` 를 부른다. 그래서 `stand_at`(fccv)·`write`·누구냐 묻기와 다시 부르기(nmv2)·쓴 뒤 커서와 알림(064q)이 전부 같다. **담기가 실패하면 적은 글은 안 폼에 열린 채 남는다** — 까닭은 배너, 고치고 Ctrl-S. 임시 파일에 두고 경로를 대는 길보다 낫다: 사람이 파일을 찾아갈 필요가 없고 버릴 때는 폼의 Esc 가 한 번 묻는다.
- 편집기가 0 이 아닌 코드로 끝나거나 못 띄우면 **담지 않고** 한 줄 알림. 제목이 비어도 담지 않고 알림. 둘 다 파일은 그대로다.

**임시 파일.** `std::env::temp_dir()` 에 `moai-idea-<pid>-<n>.md`, `create_new` + 0600(남의 눈에 안 보이게). `.md` 는 편집기가 본문을 마크다운으로 칠하게 한다. 읽고 나면 **어느 길로든 지운다**(성공·비영·못 읽음). 편집기 안에서 Ctrl-C 로 moai 가 신호에 죽으면 파일이 남는다 — 그때 터미널은 이미 내려 둔 상태라 셸은 멀쩡하다. 신호를 막으려면 `unsafe` 와 `libc` 가 들어야 해 이번에는 안 한다(vi·nano 는 raw 로 돌아 Ctrl-C 가 신호가 되지 않는다).
- 패닉: 루프 스레드는 `wait` 에 서 있어 패닉할 곳이 없다. 다시 읽기 스레드가 그 사이 터지면 훅이 raw mode 를 걷어 편집기 화면이 흐트러질 수 있다 — 드문 일이라 idea 로 남긴다. 돌아와서는 다음 `follow` 가 되던진다(r27k 그대로).

**키**: `n`(`B::Jot`) 한 줄 그대로. 새 동작·새 키 없음(hudg 의 `SPC n` 은 뒤 이슈).

title: 리뷰 — TUI 워크트리 겹쳐 보기 기본 켬 (8e26871)

탐색기 경로 줄의 '⎇ 옆 워크트리 없음  w 로 끈다' 가 겹쳐 보기 기본 켬(moai-zcuh) 뒤로 늘 선다 — 옆 워크트리가 없으면 경로 줄 절반을 먹는다. 없을 때는 안 세우거나 짧게 줄일지 정한다. git 밖 프로젝트에서 찾지 못한 까닭(Gathered::unfound)도 탐색기가 w 로 직접 켰을 때는 대지 않는다(리뷰 moai-zcuh.fqp).

text:
## /code-review high --fix 8e26871 — 원문

I found two problems in `8e26871` and fixed both. All tests pass (611 unit, 238 CLI). I couldn't file them through ReportFindings because that tool isn't available here, so the findings are listed below. Nothing is committed.

- **`src/cmd/tui.rs:26` (medium): permanent warning banner in projects that aren't git repos.** Because the overlay is now on by default, the TUI looks for git worktrees on every open, every auto-reread and every project entered from the layer. In a directory with `.moai` but no git (or on a machine without git), that lookup fails. The result is a `! 워크트리를 못 찾았다 — fatal: not a git repository …` banner every time, even though the user never asked for the overlay. Before this commit the message only appeared after pressing `w`. I reproduced the message with `moai status --worktree` in a scratch non-git repo.
  - **Fix:** `Gathered` (`src/worktree.rs`) gets a new `unfound: Option<String>` field that holds this one failure, separate from `trouble`.
  - **CLI:** `cmd::gather` still prints it, so `status`/`ready`/`show --worktree` behave as before and `worktree_trouble_is_told_but_never_fails_the_command` still passes.
  - **TUI:** both TUI reads (`cmd/tui.rs` and `prepare`) ignore it. The TUI still says `옆 워크트리 없음` in the path bar. The catch is that it no longer gives the reason, even if you turn the overlay on yourself with `w`.
- **`src/tui/mod.rs:430` (low): warnings counted twice on open.** `build` already counts warnings once (its own comment says "한 번만 센다"), and `overlaid` then ran the full `report::status` scan again. Now it only recounts when removing duplicate unreadable ids actually changed the list, which only happens when another worktree is overlaid.

One thing I noticed but left alone: in repos with no other worktrees, the `⎇ 옆 워크트리 없음  w 로 끈다` label is now always shown and takes up to half the path bar. That label is existing, deliberate behaviour, so changing it is a design call rather than a bug fix.

Changed files: src/worktree.rs, src/cmd/mod.rs, src/cmd/tui.rs, src/tui/mod.rs

판단: 둘 다 받는다. (1) git 밖 프로젝트마다 시키지 않은 배너가 서는 것은 기본 켬이 만든 회귀라 unfound 를 trouble 과 가르는 수정을 그대로 둔다. 대가로 탐색기에서 w 로 직접 켰을 때도 까닭을 안 대는데, 경로 줄이 '옆 워크트리 없음' 은 말하므로 받아들이고 moai-n468 에 담았다. CLI --worktree 는 전과 같이 stderr 로 말한다. (2) overlaid 의 경고 두 번 세기는 못 읽는 줄의 자가 바뀔 때만 다시 세도록 한 수정을 받는다. 넘긴 것: 옆 워크트리 없음 표지가 늘 경로 줄을 먹는 것 — 설계 판단이라 moai-n468 로 넘긴다. 시험 611+238 을 이쪽에서 다시 돌려 통과를 봤다.

리뷰 원문 (/code-review high --fix HEAD~1..HEAD):

HEAD~1..HEAD (moai-u7k8) 에서 correctness 버그는 찾지 못했다. 효율 한 건을 고쳤다. 빌드와 워크트리 테스트(단위 11, CLI 5)가 통과한다.

검토한 경우(모두 의도대로): theirs 가 뒤/앞, 한쪽이 rm 전에 merge, 분기점 스냅샷의 중복 id, 빈 updated_at, merge-base 없음·moai 이전 역사, 하위 디렉터리 .moai, 둘째 워크트리가 분기 후 같은 줄을 만짐.

1. 고침 — src/worktree.rs:248 (efficiency): gather 가 옆 워크트리마다 base_of(git merge-base + git show)를 불렀다. 옆 줄이 전부 여기에도 있는 흔한 경우에도 그랬고, TUI 는 다시 읽을 때마다 gather 를 지나 워크트리마다 git 두 번을 더 치렀다. 이 워크트리 id 의 HashSet 을 한 번 만들어, 옆에 여기 없는 줄이 하나라도 있을 때만 base_of 를 부른다.
2. 넘김 — src/worktree.rs:172: moai note 는 updated_at 을 안 바꾼다. 여기서 지웠고 옆에서 분기 후 note 만 붙였으면 여전히 숨는다. 고치려면 저널을 읽거나(저널은 상태 계산에 읽히지 않는다 위반) note 가 updated_at 을 올리게 해야 해서(범위 밖, 행동 변경) 설계 판단이다. idea 로 담을 만하다.
3. 넘김 — src/worktree.rs:235: TUI 는 옆 issues.jsonl 만 지켜본다. 옆 HEAD 가 움직여(커밋·merge) 분기점이 바뀌어도 다시 읽기가 일어나지 않는다. 다른 까닭으로 다시 읽을 때 반영되어 잠깐 낡은 화면에 그친다.
판단: 1 은 반영했다(fix 커밋). 2 는 moai-dyeu(idea)로 담았다 — note 가 '옆에서 만졌다' 인지는 updated_at 의 뜻을 바꾸는 설계 결정이라 사용자와 정한다. 3 은 moai-pqrq(idea)로 담았다 — 낡는 것이 다음 다시 읽기까지뿐이고 HEAD 를 지켜보려면 .git 안 ref 파일을 재야 해 지금 값어치가 작다.

text:
## 리뷰 원문 (/code-review high --fix, 브랜치 worktree-agent-ab9d88e75b2884fbe)

No correctness bugs found after reading every hunk of the editor-based jot. Two low-severity findings; one fixed.

**Findings**
1. `src/cmd/tui.rs:645` (low) — `the_scratch_file_never_reuses_an_existing_name` couldn't fail. The name counter only moves forward, so `scratch_file` never met an existing name; the test only wrote and read back its own file and would pass with the "don't open an existing file" protection removed. **Fixed:** the test pre-creates the next 8 candidate names and checks `scratch_file` picks a different name and leaves them untouched. Editor tests pass (6/6).
2. `src/cmd/tui.rs:160` (low) — the comment says saving before resume means the text is already in the file. That holds only when the save succeeds. If the save needs a name (Ask) or fails and leaves the form open, and `resume(term)?` then errors, the loop exits and the text is lost. **Not fixed:** resume almost never fails and handling it properly reaches beyond this diff.

**Checked and fine**
- Redraw after the editor: `resume` clears the screen and empties both buffers; cursor re-hidden each frame.
- Editor launch: path passed to `sh` as a positional argument; exit codes (`:cq`, 127) reach the notice.
- Temp file: create_new, 0600, deleted on every path.
- Target project fixed at open, unchanged by a layer reload.
- Template comments: a target name with newline or `\r` can't leak into the title (`one_line`).

**Noted, not acted on:** Ctrl-C while a non-raw editor runs kills moai too (already commented; git ignores SIGINT there). On Windows a set `$EDITOR` can never launch (no `sh`), making the built-in form unreachable; project doesn't target Windows.

## 판단

1. 임시 파일 이름 시험이 실패할 수 없었던 것 — 리뷰가 고친 그대로 받아 fix 커밋(50c80a9)으로 남겼다.
2. 담기가 누구냐 묻기·쓰기 실패로 폼에 남은 채 resume 이 실패하면 글을 잃는 길 — 넘긴다. resume 실패가 드물고, 고치려면 루프 끝에 복구 경로를 새로 지어야 한다 → moai-p32v.
3. 편집기 중 Ctrl-C 로 moai 가 같이 끝나는 것 — 넘긴다. 신호를 막으려면 unsafe·libc 가 들고, vi·nano 는 raw 로 돌아 신호가 나지 않는다(설계 메모에 적음). 편집기 중 다시 읽기 스레드 패닉은 moai-0l65.
4. Windows 에서 sh 가 없어 $EDITOR 가 안 뜨는 것 — 안 한다. 이 저장소는 unix 만 대상이다(훅·셸 경로 전체가 그렇다).

note: 편집기 담기 리뷰 — 이름 시험을 실패할 수 있게 고쳤고, resume 실패 시 글 잃음은 moai-p32v, 편집기 중 패닉은 moai-0l65 로 넘겼다
n 이 VISUAL·EDITOR·vi·nano 편집기로 생각을 담는다(첫 줄 제목, 안내 주석) — 편집기가 없을 때만 안 폼, 루프가 터미널을 내리고 올리며 담는 길은 폼과 한 길

text:
## moai-ob4c(vi 이동)가 남긴 것 — 이 이슈가 할 일

**아직 바로 누르는 키로 남은 것 (확정표 moai-hudg 대로 SPC 뒤로 옮길 것)**
- `f` 거름망 → `SPC f` (F7 숨은 별칭도 걷는다)
- `n` 생각 담기 → `SPC n`
- `q`·F10 끝내기 → `SPC q` — 바로 누르는 끝내기는 Ctrl-C 하나만 남긴다. `quitting_works_every_documented_way`(mod.rs)·도움말의 "F10 이나 q" · 80칸 바 시험의 `F10 끝내기` 를 함께 고친다. **`q` 가 더는 안 끝내는 것을 명시적으로 시험한다**(hudg 조건). 고르기 창의 `q` 닫기는 그대로(창 닫기, 앱은 안 끝남)
- F5·`r` 다시 읽기 → `SPC r`
- `w` 워크트리 → `SPC t w`
- F3·`m` 원문↔그리기 → `SPC t r`
- `a` 등록 → `SPC p a`, `d`·Delete 해제 → `SPC p d` (고르기 창 안의 `a` 는 바로 누르는 키로 둔다)
- 폼의 F2 → 걷는다(Ctrl-S 만)
- `/` 검색은 **바로 누르는 키로 남는다**(확정표) — 메뉴에도 같은 뜻으로 선다

**그대로 쓸 수 있는 것**
- `keys::Chord` (keys.rs) — 접두어 대기 열. `feed(table, k) -> Option<A>` 가 Run 이면 비우고, Pending 이면 들고, Unknown 이면 버린다. `App::chord`·`Picker::chord` 로 이미 든다. **SPC 메뉴는 다른 규칙이 필요하다**: 확정표는 메뉴에서 모르는 키를 "무시 — 메뉴는 그대로 떠 있다" 로 정했다. 오늘 `feed` 는 Unknown 에서 열을 버린다(gg 에 맞춘 자). 메뉴 열이면 Unknown 에서 **마지막 키만 빼고 열을 둔다** 를 고르는 모양이 필요하다 — `feed` 에 규칙 인자를 주거나, 열이 `SPC` 로 시작하면 버리지 않는 판정을 든 쪽에 둔다. Esc(버림)·Bksp(한 층 위 = 마지막 키 pop)도 여기에 붙인다
- `Chord::waiting()` 은 지금 `#[cfg(test)]` 다 — 메뉴를 그릴 때(대기 열 = 메뉴가 열렸고 어느 층인가) 풀어 쓴다. 열 자체를 읽는 접근자도 필요하다
- `keys::parse_seq` — `SPC t w`(띄어 적기)를 이미 푼다. `every_label_is_the_key_it_names`·도움말 시험이 이것으로 열 이름을 잰다
- 붙여넣기·글칸으로 넘어간 모드가 열을 버리는 자리(`App::paste`·`App::key` 의 `!Browse` 가지)가 이미 있다 — 메뉴가 열린 채 붙여넣기면 메뉴가 닫힌다
- `no_row_is_shadowed_or_a_prefix_of_another` — SPC 열을 더할 때 SPC 한 키 동작이 없어야 한다. 옛 SPC·`b`(상세 한 쪽)는 ob4c 에서 이미 걷었다

**ob4c 가 정해 두고 넘긴 것**
- 드나들기의 이름은 `Enter`·`Bksp`, `h`·`l` 은 숨은 별칭이다 — 80칸 바가 빠듯하고 층의 거절문이 한 키만 대야 해서. F10·F5·F3 이 바에서 빠지면 자리가 나니 `h·l` 을 바에 세울지 다시 본다
- `g` 를 누르고 기다리는 동안 화면에 아무 표시가 없다. SPC 메뉴가 대기 열을 그리게 되면 `g` 도 같은 자리(바)에 대기 표시를 세울지 본다

note: vi 이동을 표에 더했다(768a8ac) — j·k·gg·G·Ctrl-d/u/f/b 가 포커스 칸을, h·l 이 드나들기를. j·k 의 상세 굴리기와 SPC·b 는 걷었고 창의 경로 적기는 g p. 대기 열은 keys::Chord. SPC 로 옮길 키는 moai-7sjm note

text:
## 결정: 들어가면 `..` 너머 첫 줄에 선다 (디렉터리·프로젝트 모두)

**무엇**: `App::first_row` 하나가 정한다 — 줄이 둘 이상이고 첫 줄이 `..` 이면 1, 아니면 0(빈 디렉터리는 `..` 뿐이라 거기). `enter`(에픽·마일스톤 디렉터리)·`enter_project`(층의 프로젝트, 들이기 **뒤에** 세운다 — `take` 가 커서를 정체 `..` 로 붙들므로)·`with_layer`(안에서 띄운 첫 화면, 옛 `cursor = 1` 을 같은 함수로) 셋이 같은 자를 읽는다.

**왜**
- `..` 에 세우면 들어가자마자 누른 Enter(·`l`) 한 번이 도로 나와 **Enter 두 번이 제자리다**(흡수한 moai-o8q8 의 증상). 들어간 사람이 먼저 보려는 것은 안의 줄이다
- 이미 두 곳이 그렇게 서 있었다 — 고르기 창(`Picker::new` 는 첫 하위 디렉터리)과 `with_layer`. 셋째 자리만 달랐다
- `..` 에 세워 두던 값(나가는 길을 보인다)은 vi 키(moai-ob4c)로 사라졌다 — `h`·Bksp·← 가 어느 줄에서든 나가고, `..` 은 `k`·`gg`·Home 한 번 거리다

**못 박던 시험을 고쳤다**: `layer.rs` `entering_and_leaving_keeps_each_projects_lines_apart` 가 "들어가면 `..` 에 선다" 를 결정으로 박고 있었다 — 이제 `cursor == 1` 을 재고 까닭을 주석에 적었다(옛 커서의 id 를 안 따라가는 것은 그대로 잰다). 새 시험 `entering_lands_past_the_up_row`(mod.rs): 들어가면 첫 줄, 곧바로 Enter 는 안 나감, `k` 한 번에 `..`, 빈 디렉터리는 `..`.

**함께 고친 시험**: draw.rs 에서 "Enter 뒤 ↓ 로 첫 줄" 을 누르던 12곳의 ↓ 를 뺐다. `..` 에 선 채로 재던 둘(`adopt` 의 `..` 붙들기, 빛줄기 시험)은 Home 으로 `..` 에 올라간다.

**안 바꾼 것**: 나올 때(`leave`)는 그대로 방금 나온 디렉터리에 선다. 되돌아와 선 자리를 붙드는 `remembered` 도 그대로다.

note: 들어가면 `..` 너머 첫 줄에 선다 — enter·enter_project·with_layer 가 App::first_row 한 자를 읽는다. 못 박던 layer.rs 시험을 까닭과 함께 고쳤다

text:
## 리뷰 원문 — /code-review high --fix main...HEAD (@code-review-2)

I reviewed `main...HEAD` (vi movement for moai-ob4c, cursor on entering for moai-cm13) and found one real problem, a stale doc comment, which I fixed. The `ReportFindings` tool isn't available in this session, so the findings are listed here. The TUI tests pass (`cargo test --bin moai tui`: 239 passed, 1 ignored). I didn't run `cargo fmt`.

**Finding**
- `src/tui/register.rs:18` — low — The doc comment on `SHOWN_MAX` still said the path-entry key is `g`. The picker table now uses `g p`, and a lone `g` only waits for the next key. Someone following this comment would press `g` in a directory with more than 2000 entries and nothing would happen. **Fixed:** changed `` `g`(경로 적기) `` to `` `g p`(경로 적기) ``.

**Checked and found fine**
- **Changed key meanings:** `j`·`k` now move the focused pane, SPC and `b` do nothing, and the picker's `g` became `g p`. All three are deliberate and covered by tests. The on-screen hints match: the detail pane shows `(Tab)` from the list and `(j·k)` in the detail pane, and the bar's `Step` label switches between 이동 and 굴리기 with focus.
- **Pending `g` leaking:**
  - Switching to a text-field mode clears it (`App::key`), and so does paste, in both the app and the picker.
  - Actions that open or close the picker, enter or leave a layer, reload, or switch focus are all triggered by a key. That key either completes the sequence or throws away the pending `g`, so it can't carry over.
  - A new picker starts with an empty sequence, and `relist`/`show` don't bring one back.
  - Reloads from file changes don't clear it, but the leftover `g` is one the user actually typed, so that's harmless.
  - Key-release events are already filtered out in `cmd/tui.rs:318`, so a press plus release of `g` can't count as `gg`.
- **Letters in text fields:** in search, filter and the picker's path field, `g`·`j`·`k`·`h`·`l`·`G` are typed as letters, because typing is handled before the key sequence is looked at.
- **`Key::chord`:** Ctrl-d/u/f/b match only without Alt, SHIFT is ignored for letters, and they don't clash with Ctrl-C (Anywhere table) or Ctrl-S (idea form).
- **`first_row`:** it lands on `..` in an empty or filtered-out directory. On the project layer there's no `..` row, so it gives 0. `with_layer` behaves as before, and `enter_project` sets the cursor after `apply_fresh`, so the cursor-keeping logic can't undo it.
- **Help text:** the `cli.rs` help and the `draw.rs` key bar agree with the key tables.

**Not reported (intended):** a `g` followed by an unmapped key (Esc, `q`, F10) drops both keys. So `g` then Esc doesn't clear the filter, and `g` then `q` doesn't quit. This is what the design says and the tests check it.

## 판단

**반영**
- `register.rs` `SHOWN_MAX` 주석의 옛 키 `g` → `g p` — 리뷰가 고친 그대로 받았다(fix 커밋).

**반영하지 않은 것과 까닭**
- "`g` 뒤의 Esc·`q` 도 버려진다" — 리뷰도 의도로 적었다. 확정표(moai-hudg)의 "모르는 키 무시" 와 같은 자이고 시험(`an_unknown_key_after_g_is_ignored_and_clears_the_wait`)이 잰다. 그대로 둔다.
- "파일 바뀜으로 인한 다시 읽기는 기다리는 `g` 를 안 버린다" — 남은 `g` 는 사람이 친 것이고 `gg` 는 맨 위로 가는 무해한 동작이라 그대로 둔다.

**넘긴 것 (이슈 번호와 함께)**
- `g` 를 누르고 기다리는 동안 화면에 대기 표시가 없다 — SPC 메뉴가 대기 열을 그리게 되는 moai-7sjm 에 note 로 넘겼다(같은 자리에서 한 번에 푼다).
- 드나들기의 바 이름에 `h·l` 을 세울지 — F키가 바에서 빠지는 moai-7sjm 에 넘겼다.
- 머지 뒤 한 번 흔들린 시험 `outside_a_repo_each_project_wears_its_own_colour…`(이 작업과 무관, main 에서 온 것) — idea moai-tcqp.

title: --worktree: 옆에서 defer 한 것이 여기서 먼저 옮긴 칸에 가려진다 — defer 는 status_since 를 안 올려 겹칠 때 안 이긴다 (moai-q65n.xi1)

text:
리뷰 원문 (/code-review high --fix HEAD~1..HEAD, ba63873):

HEAD~1..HEAD 에서 실제 버그는 찾지 못해 --fix 가 바꿀 것이 없었다.

바뀐 것: --worktree 가 같은 이슈를 두 워크트리에서 보이면 overlay(src/worktree.rs:172) 가 칸을 가장 늦게 옮긴 줄(status_since)을 세운다. 같을 때만 updated_at, 완전 동률이면 이 브랜치의 줄.

검토:
- 규칙은 옳다. status_since 는 칸이 실제로 바뀔 때만 선다(src/cmd/mv.rs:69 는 같은 칸으로의 이동을 건너뛰고, src/cmd/idea.rs:133 은 idea 를 펼칠 때 세운다). 필드 편집·defer 는 안 건드린다.
- 옛 줄은 안전하다. status_since 는 필수 필드라 빈 문자열이 비교에서 지는 경우가 없다.
- 에픽·마일스톤은 괜찮다. 칸이 겹친 뒤 멤버에서 계산되므로 제 status_since 는 상관없다.
- 지운 줄 검사는 그대로다(177행). merge-base 스냅샷과 updated_at 으로 견주는 것이 옳다 — 저쪽에서 집거나 고치면 둘 다 updated_at 을 올린다.
- 새 시험 둘 다 옛 결함을 잡는다. CLI 시험에서 옛 규칙이면 09-13 의 편집이 09-12 의 이동을 이겨 ready 가 집힌 일을 다시 냈다. 모든 ok 호출이 MOAI_NOW 를 고정한다.
- cargo test --release worktree: 단위 12, CLI 6 통과.

절충 하나(버그 아님): defer 도 status_since 를 안 바꾸므로 늦은 defer 가 가려질 수 있다. 여기서 T1 에 집고 옆에서 T2 에 미루면 status --worktree 는 여기 in_progress 줄을 보이고 미룬 것을 안 보인다. 이 커밋 전에는 미룬 것이 보였다. "칸을 늦게 옮긴 줄이 통째로" 를 일부러 고른 결과다. ready 는 영향이 없다 — 여기서 진행 중인 일은 어차피 안 낸다.
판단: 고칠 버그 없음. defer 가 status_since 를 안 올려 옆의 늦은 defer 가 가려지는 절충은 moai-bh3h(idea)로 담았다 — defer 를 칸 이동처럼 셀지는 '미루기는 칸이 아니다' 축 결정과 닿아 사용자와 정한다.

note: 버그 없음, defer 가려짐 절충은 moai-bh3h 로 넘겼다

## 리뷰 원문 — 리뷰 서브에이전트(high), main...worktree-moai-0l65 (b7bc5f6)

(워크트리 안에서는 훅 규칙 3 이 본 저장소의 리뷰 이슈를 못 봐 /code-review 가 막혀, 사용자 선택으로 같은 관점의 서브에이전트가 봤다 — idea moai-iz38)

I found no deadlock and no bug in the Gate itself. The fix does what it claims for a panic that starts after `hold()`. It still has one narrow ordering hole that can leave the shell raw and on the alternate screen, and one weaker side effect. Tests: `cargo test --bin moai cmd::tui` passed 8/8 on three runs, 0.15s each.

**Findings, most severe first**

1. **Medium (rare): a panic just before `n` still leaves the terminal raw and on the alternate screen.**
   - Where: `src/cmd/tui.rs:309` (the hook's `EDITING.wait()`), `src/cmd/tui.rs:398` (`hold()`), `src/cmd/tui.rs:548` (`resume`).
   - What's wrong: the gate only stops hooks that reach `wait()` after `hold()`. A hook that got past `wait()` first has already restored the terminal. Nothing on the loop side knows that, so `resume()` switches raw mode and the alternate screen back on. The next `follow()` or `reap()` joins the dead thread and calls `resume_unwind`, which skips the hook. `screen()`'s `ratatui::restore()` at line 184 isn't a drop guard, so it never runs either.
   - Scenario:
     1. While a read is pending (`LOAD_POLL`, so at most ~30ms per step), a reader thread panics during `event::poll`.
     2. Its hook runs in full (paste off, restore, message printed).
     3. In the same step, `poll` returns the `n` key, and `suspend()` calls `hold()` too late.
     4. The user writes in vi and quits. `resume()` turns raw mode and the alternate screen back on, then `release()`.
     5. `follow()` sees `Disconnected`, joins, and calls `resume_unwind`. The process exits with code 101, the shell is raw and on the alternate screen, and the panic message is hidden on the main screen.
   - The window is also open if the panic comes any time after the last `follow()` but before `hold()`. Note the call-site comment at 545-547 describes exactly this bad end state; it just only considers the release-first ordering.
   - Fix: wrap `loop_until_quit` in `screen()` so terminal teardown doesn't depend on the hook (catch_unwind → paste off → ratatui::restore → resume_unwind). This covers all four rethrow sites (`src/tui/mod.rs:701`, `:721`, `:969`, `src/tui/layer.rs:616`) and every ordering. Keep the gate; it is still what keeps the hook from wrecking vi's screen.

2. **Low: after `release()`, the forced full redraw likely overwrites the panic message.**
   - Where: `src/cmd/tui.rs:549`, together with `resume()`'s `swap_buffers()` at line 416.
   - What's wrong: `release()` wakes the waiting hook at exactly the moment the loop starts its next step, and `swap_buffers()` has made that step repaint every cell. The hook then disables raw mode, leaves the alternate screen and prints, while the loop paints a whole frame with absolute cursor moves. `follow()` still sees `Empty` (the sender lives until unwinding ends), so the loop keeps drawing about 30ms before the rethrow. The frame can land on the main screen over the message.
   - Outside the editor the same race exists, but only changed cells (the spinner) are drawn, so the damage is small. The Gate comment "편집기 밖에서 터진 것과 같은 차례가 된다" is true for the final terminal state, not for what the user ends up seeing.
   - Fix: in the `catch_unwind` path from finding 1, after `restore()`, print the payload again (downcast to `&str`/`String`) so it is the last thing on screen. Or at least soften the comment.

3. **Nit: the comments state the guarantee without its precondition.**
   - Where: `src/cmd/tui.rs:395-396` (`suspend` doc) and the Gate doc at 321-324.
   - "그 스레드가 터지면 훅은 EDITING 앞에서 선다" holds only for panics that start after `hold()`. If finding 1 isn't fixed, add that, since the call-site comment implies every ordering is covered.

4. **Nit: the test covers the Gate but not how it's wired in.**
   - Where: `src/cmd/tui.rs:625`.
   - Nothing would catch the hook losing its `wait()` call, or `release()` moving above `resume()`. That is acceptable, since the wiring needs a TTY.
   - The 150ms check is not flaky in the failing direction: a slow scheduler can only make it pass wrongly, never fail. The 5s wake-up bound is generous. No change needed.

**Checked and fine**

- Lost or spurious wakeups: `release` sets `None` under the lock and then calls `notify_all`, and `wait` re-checks in a `while` loop.
- Poisoning: no code that can panic runs while the Gate lock is held. `into_inner` in the hook is still the right defence.
- Loop thread panicking between `hold` and `release` (e.g. in `app.edited` → `save_idea` → `write`): the hook sees itself as holder and doesn't wait; the process exits with 101 and any hook still waiting dies with it.
- `resume_unwind` between `hold` and `release`: `discard`/`reap` joins only threads where `is_finished()` is true, so a thread stuck in the hook can't be joined there — no deadlock.
- Waiting thread still holding locks: readers never take the store `flock`; no global Mutex/RwLock/OnceLock statics contended.
- `resume()` failing: gate still released, `up?` returns, `screen()` restores, woken hook restores again. Harmless.
- Other exits: Ctrl-C during a non-raw editor kills the process; an editor left open forever keeps the hook waiting forever, which is intended.
- Comment at 545-547: accurate about why `release` comes after `resume`.
- Hook order: `paste_off_on_panic` still installed after `try_init`.

규칙 2 도 같다(2026-09-14): 본 저장소에서 moai-46xe.jxd 를 in_progress 로 둔 채 워크트리 moai-0l65 의 src/cmd/tui.rs 를 Edit 하자 '집은 것 없이 고치고 있다' 로 막혔다. 워크트리의 .moai 는 브랜치 HEAD 스냅샷이라 본 저장소에서 만들고 집은 이슈가 없다. 워크트리에서 일하는 흐름 전체가 훅에 막힌다.

/code-review high --fix 8bdbd5b 원문

I found no real bugs in `8bdbd5b`, and the uncommitted `src/view.rs` change is also fine, so `--fix` had nothing to apply. The ReportFindings tool isn't in this session, so there was no tool call; this is the whole report. The full test suite passes (`cargo test --release`: 640 unit and 241 CLI tests, 0 failed).

What I checked in `src/report.rs`, the TUI files and the `view.rs` change:

- **`Stand::aside`:** it's only filled when the epic or milestone counts as `done`. Every member that counted toward that is already done, so any unfinished member must be one that was left out as deferred. Members come from `members_in`, which lists work items only, so no epic's stored status can slip into the list.
- **The `blocker` order:** `aside` wins over `Done`, and it can only be true when the column is `done`. The new branch therefore can't change any other outcome.
- **Where `deferred_roots_in` drops a group:** a group can't be both taken out of the plan and done with deferred members aside, so the plain deferred path and the new one never overlap. In the TUI, `app.aside` and `app.index.deferred_root` agree for the same reason.
- **`held`:** listing members instead of the group still gives the right `--undo` target. A member deferred through its parent, its epic or a milestone points back to that item, and duplicates are removed.
- **Other places that decide "blocked":** `ready`, `held`, the `status` warnings and the TUI detail panel all go through the single `report::blocker` function. None of `query`, `hook` or `cmd` checks the column by hand.
- **`src/view.rs` (uncommitted):** `projects_ready` now prints the problem lines after the "N건 더" tail, which is the same order `projects_status` uses. The count is unchanged.

There's one thing I left alone because it's cosmetic, not a bug. In `src/tui/draw.rs` (around line 1047), the "미룬 멤버" line lists every deferred member with no limit. If you defer a whole large epic inside a milestone, that line gets long, and since it's cut from the right the group's title disappears.

text:
## moai-7sjm(SPC 메뉴)가 바에 남긴 것

**지금 바** (src/tui/draw.rs `browse_hints`)
- 프로젝트 안: 떨어지는 차례대로 `j·k` · `Tab` · `/ 검색` · `Bksp 나가기` · `Enter 들어가기`, 늘 남는 것 `Esc 풀기`(거름망이 걸렸을 때) · `SPC 메뉴`
- 층: `j·k` · `Tab` · `Enter`, 늘 남는 것 `SPC 메뉴`
- 메뉴가 열린 동안: `Esc 닫기`, 하위 층이면 `Bksp 위로`
- 80칸 목록 포커스에서 거름망이 걸려도 68칸이라 하나도 안 떨어진다(`the_key_bar_fits_whole_at_eighty_columns`)

**이 이슈가 정할 것**
- **`h·l` 을 바에 세울지.** 자리는 난다(80칸에 12칸 남음). 다만 층의 거절문이 `label(BROWSE, Enter)` 로 "Enter 로 들어가서" 를 대므로, 이름을 `Enter·l` 로 늘리면 문구도 같이 는다 — 바에만 따로 적는 길을 고른다면 `every_key_on_the_browse_bar_is_an_enabled_row_of_the_table` 가 이름을 키로 풀어 보므로 그대로 지난다
- **`Ctrl-C 끝내기` 를 바에 세울지.** 지금은 메뉴의 `q  끝내기` 와 `moai tui --help` 만 댄다. 늘 남는 묶음에 넣으면 80칸 거름망 켠 목록 포커스에서 `j·k` 가 떨어진다(82칸)
- **`g` 대기 표시.** `gg` 의 첫 `g` 를 누르고 기다리는 동안 화면에 표시가 없다. 대기 열은 `app.chord.held()` 로 읽을 수 있고(`menu::open` 이 거짓이고 열이 비지 않으면 `g` 대기), 메뉴가 바를 `Esc 닫기` 로 갈아 끼우는 `fkeys` 의 첫 가지와 같은 자리에 `g …` 한 칸을 세우면 된다. 7sjm 에서는 바의 차례를 이 이슈에 맡기려고 넣지 않았다
- 바의 모양이 바뀌면 `the_key_bar_still_names_the_menu_at_eighty_columns`·`the_key_bar_fits_whole_at_eighty_columns`·`the_menu_reads_without_colour_at_eighty_columns` 를 함께 본다

title: TUI 가 화면에 보이는 줄에 도는 것이 있을 때만 빠른 걸음으로 깨운다 — 안 보이는 집은 일로 다시 그리지 않는다
에픽·마일스톤 줄에도 빛줄기 — 밑에 집은 일이 있을 때(도는 묶음)

text: 결정 1 (커서에서 되는 키, uowi 흡수): keys::Ctx 에 leaf·root 를 더하고 Browse::enabled 가 잎의 Enter·뿌리의 Bksp 를 Off::Quiet 로 끈다. 바에서 빠지는 것과 키가 아무 일도 안 하는 것이 한 판정이다. root = path 가 비었고 (층이 없거나 층에 섰다) — 층이 있는 프로젝트 뿌리는 Bksp 가 climb 하므로 뿌리가 아니다. leaf = 커서 줄이 ..·디렉터리·프로젝트가 아니다(App::enter 가 무언가 하는 줄). key_ctx 는 rows 를 받는다: 커서 줄을 알려면 목록을 세야 하고(이슈 전부 훑고 정렬), 그림은 프레임에 센 것을 넘기며 키 처리는 키당 한 번 세어 step 에도 준다. 흔들림(uowi 의 걱정): 80칸 거름망 켠 목록에서도 하나도 안 떨어지므로 빠지는 Enter·Bksp 말고는 칸이 제자리다 — the_key_bar_keeps_its_order_as_the_cursor_moves_at_eighty_columns 가 바를 통째로 견준다.
결정 2 (h·l): 바에 안 세운다. 드나들기의 이름은 Enter·Bksp 하나로 둔다 — 바를 짧게, 층의 거절문이 'Enter 로 들어가서' 한 키만 대게. h·l 은 moai tui --help 가 댄다. 바의 gone 목록에 h·/·l 을 더해 묶었다.
결정 3 (Ctrl-C 끝내기): 바에 안 세운다. 메뉴가 'q 끝내기' 를 대고 도움말이 Ctrl-C 를 댄다. 늘 남는 묶음에 넣으면 80칸 거름망 켠 목록 포커스에서 j·k 가 떨어진다(82칸). 바의 gone 목록에 Ctrl-C 를 더했다.

결정 4 (g 대기 표시): 넣는다. chord 가 g 를 들고 있고 메뉴가 아니면 메뉴가 서는 바 자리를 ' g → g 맨 위' 로 갈아 끼운다(고르기 창은 ' g → g 맨 위 · p 경로 적기'). 이어 누를 키는 keys::next_keys 가 표에서 읽는다 — 이름 붙은 줄만, 탐색은 enabled 로 거른다. 이동의 낱말은 keys::move_word. 열이 비면(gg 든 뜻 없는 키든) 바가 돌아온다. 메뉴 창은 안 뜬다.

note: 루프는 방금 그린 버퍼에 스피너 글자가 있을 때만 빠른 걸음으로 깬다(App::spun) — 스크롤 밖·폼에 덮인 줄로 안 깨고, 상세에만 선 건수로는 깬다. App::spinning 은 걷었다

text: 결정: 마일스톤 줄도 에픽과 같은 규칙이다 — 빛줄기는 App::spins 하나를 따르고, 마일스톤은 묶음이라 밑(에픽을 거쳐 물려받은 멤버 포함)에 집은 일이 실제로 있을 때만 돌고 빛난다. 따로 가르면 도는 마일스톤이 글리프만 돌고 빛은 없어 한 화면에 규칙이 둘이 된다. 프로젝트 층의 프로젝트 줄은 범위 밖으로 두었다(그 줄은 글리프도 안 돈다).

note: 빛줄기는 App::spins 하나를 따른다 — 집은 일을 품은 에픽·마일스톤도 흐르고, 첫 칸뿐이거나 집은 멤버를 미룬 묶음은 안 흐른다. draw.rs 의 묶음 가지를 걷었다

/code-review high --fix 67f5746 원문

I found one real bug in 67f5746 and fixed it in the working tree. Nothing is staged or committed. I read through the rest of the diff and found nothing else worth reporting. The ReportFindings tool isn't available in this session, so the findings are listed here only.

**Finding**
- `src/report.rs:672` (`blocker`), also `holding` near line 1356 and `src/tui/draw.rs:1049` — medium. Take an epic that is itself deferred, has no finished members, and whose members were also each deferred. Before this commit, `ready` named the epic, and `moai defer <epic> --undo` cleared the block in one step. Now "all members deferred" is checked before the group's own deferral, so `ready` names the members instead. Undoing them doesn't clear the block, and `ready` then names the epic. The TUI detail says "미룬 멤버" in the same case. That goes against the commit's own rule that a group's own deferral comes first. I reproduced it on a throwaway repo:
  - **Before the fix:** `ready` printed `moai defer r1-ip17 r1-no2v --undo`, and after those two it still printed `moai defer r1-y2r3 --undo`.
  - **After the fix:** `ready` prints `moai defer r1-y2r3 --undo` straight away.

**Fixes applied (only inside the commit's hunks)**
- **`blocker`:** a new check `Some(c) if out_of_plan && c != DONE => Blocker::Deferred` now runs before the all-deferred-members check. Groups whose members are all done are never counted as deferred, so the moai-0gxf case still comes out the same.
- **`holding`:** it names the deferred members only when the group itself is not deferred, and names the group otherwise.
- **`draw.rs`:** the "미룬 멤버" branch now also requires `root.is_none()`.
- **Test:** I added a case to `a_group_with_nothing_live_to_wait_on_says_why_it_blocks` for a group that is deferred and whose members are all deferred, plus a table row `blocker(Some("todo"), true, Waiting::Shelved) == Deferred`.

**Checks:** `cargo test --bins` passes (656), and `ready_names_an_empty_group_that_blocks` passes.

**Heads-up on the shared checkout:** `src/tui/draw.rs` now shows as `MM`. Another session's staged changes are there, and my one-line edit sits unstaged on top of them. Check that before anyone runs `git add` on that file. My other edit is in `src/report.rs`, also unstaged.

**Skipped:** nothing. The rest of the diff reads correctly:
- the `Waiting` calculation
- the widened early return in `held`
- the `status` warnings
- the hint `moai link <group> --unblocks <work>`
- how the TUI gets its data

구현에서 고친 것(첫 노트와 다르다): planned_at 은 defer·--undo 만 적는다. mv·idea promote 는 안 적는다 — 칸 이동 시각은 status_since 가 이미 말하고, 겹칠 때 Issue::planned() = max(status_since, planned_at) 로 견주므로 결과가 같다. 그 편이 매 mv 마다 줄에 필드를 하나 더 얹지 않고, 옛 바이너리가 칸만 옮긴 줄(낡은 planned_at + 늦은 status_since)도 옳게 선다. 필드가 없는 줄은 바이트가 그대로다(skip_serializing_if).

## 리뷰 원문 — 리뷰 서브에이전트(high), main...worktree-moai-planned (622c317)

(워크트리 안에서는 훅 규칙 3 이 본 저장소의 리뷰 이슈를 못 봐 /code-review 가 막혀, 앞서 사용자가 고른 대로 같은 관점의 서브에이전트가 봤다 — idea moai-iz38)

I found no correctness bug in the change itself: the overlay logic and serialization are sound and `cargo test` passes (644 + 242, 0 failed). What needs fixing is in the tests. The part that actually writes `planned_at` has no test at all, and one of the three new overlay cases would pass on the old code.

**Findings, most serious first**

1. **Medium (test gap): nothing checks that `defer` / `defer --undo` writes `planned_at`.** (src/cmd/defer.rs:62)
   - `planned_at` appears nowhere in tests/cli.rs, and the unit test in worktree.rs sets it by hand.
   - If someone deletes `i.planned_at = Some(at.clone());`, every test stays green and moai-l11z quietly comes back.
   - Fix: add a CLI test that runs `defer` then `defer --undo` with `MOAI_NOW` and checks the line has `"planned_at":"<t>"` both times. An end-to-end version would be better still: two worktrees, `mv` in one, a later `defer` in the other, then `ready --worktree`.

2. **Medium (test quality): the second case in `a_later_defer_or_undo_beats_an_earlier_move` proves nothing.** (src/worktree.rs:461-465)
   - The helper `issue()` (worktree.rs:345) fixes `status_since` at 2026-09-10 for every line. So `shelved` and `back` have the same `status_since`, and `back` wins on `updated_at` (t3 > t2) even with the old key. (Checked by reasoning, not by running.)
   - Fix: make the undo lose on status time. Give the local line `status_since = t2` and `updated_at = t2`, give the sibling's undo `planned_at = t3` with its `status_since` left earlier, and check the sibling wins. The first and third cases do tell old and new apart.

3. **Low: an old binary treats `planned_at` as an unknown field, which makes noise when builds are mixed.**
   - Nothing is lost: kept in `rest` and written back. But the old binary writes `rest` after `body`, so the key moves back and forth between old and new builds — repeated diff churn.
   - `--undo` never clears `planned_at`, so the old binary's `unknown_field` warning stays on every issue ever deferred.
   - Known cost of adding any field; ends once branches merge. Worth a line in the commit message; no code change needed.

4. **Low (mixed versions): an old binary's `defer` / `--undo` leaves `planned_at` stale.**
   - New binary defers at t2; old binary `--undo` at t4 (keeps planned_at = t2); sibling `mv` at t3 wins though the undo was later. Same as before the fix, no regression, can't be fixed from the new side.

5. **Low (design question, not a bug): repeating `defer` on an already-deferred line writes nothing** (defer.rs:46-56).
   - Deferred here at t1; sibling (not deferred) `mv` at t2 wins; user here runs `defer` again at t3 — "already deferred", sibling still wins. Only `--undo` then `defer` re-asserts.
   - Leaving `deferred_at` alone is right (age must not reset). Bumping only `planned_at` would bend the no-op contract. Keep current behaviour, but record the limit.

6. **Nit: the key-order tests don't cover the new fields.** `full_line_keeps_declared_key_order` (model.rs:655) doesn't include `deferred_at` or `planned_at`; no byte round-trip test for a line with `planned_at`. Checked by hand that it holds.

**Checked and fine**
- Serialization: declared position matches output; old lines unchanged; `normalize()` doesn't touch it.
- "Derived value" rule: not violated — a fact about its own line, written only to that line.
- Write paths: `defer.rs:59` is the only non-test place setting `deferred_at`.
- Multi-id defer; inherited deferral (`--undo` on a member of a deferred epic goes through the no-write branch, right).
- Overlay rules: field edits still can't beat a later move; later `mv` beats earlier deferral; ties unchanged; duplicate ids unfolded; rm-revival check still uses `updated_at` (a sibling deferral after the fork brings the line back, matching the rule); old-binary move after new-binary deferral wins via max.
- Other recency comparisons (worktree.rs:314, query.rs:65-72) mean different things; none should switch.
- JSON output: `show --json` now includes `planned_at`; no test/doc lists keys. guide.rs and plugin commands.md agree.

## 리뷰 원문 — /code-review high --fix 7d44819

I reviewed `7d44819` and found no real bugs, so `--fix` had nothing to change. The ReportFindings tool isn't available in this session, so this reply is the report.

The whole TUI test suite passes (`cargo test --release tui::`: 275 passed, 0 failed).

**What I checked:**
- **Enter and Bksp still do what they did.** The new `leaf` and `root` values in `key_ctx` (`src/tui/mod.rs`) switch a key off in exactly the places where `App::enter` or `App::leave` would do nothing:
  - **Enter:** `enter` only acts on `..`, a directory or a layer project. On any other row, or when the cursor is past the end of the list, it does nothing, and that is exactly when `leaf` is true.
  - **Bksp:** at a project root, `leave` calls `climb`. That returns early when there is no layer, or when you are already on the layer, which is exactly when `root` is true.

  A root with a layer still gets Bksp, and its `..` row still gets Enter. The only visible change is the key bar.
- **No refusal message is lost.** The two new "do nothing silently" rules in `Browse::enabled` sit after the list-focus rule and hide no older rule that gave a reason. No reason message for Enter or Bksp ever existed.
- **Counting the list once is safe.**
  - **Key handling:** `key` counts the rows once and reuses them for the move, because nothing changes the list or cursor in between.
  - **Drawing:** `screen` never changes `cursor`, so the bar, the menu and the worktree badge all see the same cursor row as the list panel.
- **The waiting `g` bar can't come out empty.**
  - **Browse:** its only follow-up is `g g` (jump to top), which is never switched off, so the bar always has something to show.
  - **Picker:** an error message still takes the bar first. A key with no meaning clears the pending `g` in both panes, and the tests cover that.
- **`next_keys` skips hidden aliases** and removes duplicate key names, as intended.

/code-review high --fix 32bc83a 원문

I found 2 real bugs in 32bc83a, both in `report::deferred_sources`, and fixed both in the working tree. My edits have since been swept into another session's commit, and that session is still changing the same function.

**Findings**
1. `src/report.rs:181` (medium): the list of deferrals to undo can name the same epic twice. When a child and its parent sit in the same deferred epic, the lookup finds that epic once from each. I reproduced it with a real binary: `moai mv <child> in_progress` printed ``E · E 를 미뤄 둬서 … `moai defer E E --undo` ``. The `--json` output also got a `"roots":[E,E]` field that should not appear when there is only one deferral.
2. `src/report.rs:183` (medium): the list can come out empty. It drops deferrals from groups that count as done, but if that was the only deferral, the row is still out of the plan with nothing left to name. Example: a deferred milestone whose only work item is done, holding an epic with no members. `moai defer <epic> --undo` printed ``를 미뤄 둬서 … `moai defer  --undo` `` (no id), and JSON printed `"root":""`. Before this commit it named the milestone.

**What I changed** (only `src/report.rs`; nothing staged or committed)
- **`deferred_sources` (about lines 181–199):** repeated ids are dropped, keeping nearest-first order. If the list would be empty, it falls back to the nearest deferral, which is what `deferred_roots` names.
- **Test `every_deferral_that_keeps_a_row_out_is_named` (about lines 2912–2927):** added two checks, one for a child and parent in the same epic and one for an empty epic under a milestone that counts as done.

**Verification:** I ran this in a separate copy of 32bc83a with its own build folder, because the shared working tree didn't compile at the time (another session's half-done edits in `src/cmd/edit.rs`). The 90 `report::` unit tests and the 17 matching CLI tests passed. Rerunning both reproductions gave correct output: ``moai defer <epic> --undo`` and ``moai defer <milestone> --undo``.

**Where things stand now:** commit `d52b7c5` (moai-ha03, from another session) already includes my change. That session is now editing the same function again, uncommitted. It drops the done-group filter entirely: the nearest deferral always comes first, so the list can't be empty and the fallback isn't needed. It keeps the de-duplication and adds a test for a deferred epic inside a deferred milestone that counts as done. That covers both findings, so I left it alone.

No other callers needed changes (`mv`, `defer`, `held`, `view::shelved_by`, the `Shelved` JSON output).

판단: 지적 둘(같은 묶음을 두 번 댐, 목록이 비어 'moai defer  --undo' 를 댐) 모두 받아들였다. 리뷰가 고친 중복 거르기와 빈 목록 대비가 커밋 전에 공유 체크아웃의 report.rs 에 있었고, moai-ha03 을 경로 커밋(git commit -- src/report.rs)으로 담으며 d52b7c5 에 함께 들어갔다 — 그 커밋 메시지에는 안 적혔다. 이어 moai-ha03 리뷰(moai-ha03.qlr)가 그 대비의 뿌리(done 으로 읽은 묶음의 미룸을 거르는 것)를 걷어 냈고, 그 수정은 뒤이은 fix 커밋으로 담는다. 넘긴 것 없음.

/code-review high --fix d52b7c5 원문

I found one real bug in d52b7c5 and fixed it in the working tree. Nothing is staged or committed.

**Finding**
- `src/report.rs:188` — `deferred_sources` leaves out a deferred group whose column reads done, even though rows under it are still out of plan because of it.
  - Example: milestone M is deferred and reads done (its only counted member is a finished issue). Epic E sits in M and is also deferred, and issue X is a todo in E.
  - The hint for X names only E. After `moai defer E --undo`, X is still out of plan (M is now its nearest deferral) and only then is M named.
  - That is the "one at a time" problem moai-phzi/g2a1 set out to remove. The `every.is_empty()` fallback added in this commit only patched the case where the list came out empty.
  - I confirmed this with a probe on a clean copy of d52b7c5.

**Fix** (only `src/report.rs`, only inside this commit's hunks)
- **Lines 183–197 (`deferred_sources`):** removed the `roots.contains_key(r)` filter and kept only the de-duplication. The hint now lists every deferral on the row's path, nearest first. That makes the `is_empty` fallback and the `nearest` binding unnecessary, so I removed them and put a comment in their place.
- **Lines 2973–2984 (test `every_deferral_that_keeps_a_row_out_is_named`):** added the M/E/X/D case, which expects `["argos-00ee", "argos-00mm"]`.

**Checks**
- On a clean copy of d52b7c5 with the fix applied, `cargo test` passed: 659 unit tests and 243 CLI tests.
- In the shared checkout, the changed test passes. I built there with a separate target directory, so `target/` was not touched.

**Left as is**
- The doc comment at `src/report.rs:172-173` still says the undo hint skips groups that read done, which is now wrong. It belongs to 32bc83a rather than d52b7c5, and another review may be editing that area, so I didn't change it. Whoever owns 32bc83a should update it.
- The rest of the commit looks correct:
  - **Ordering in `ready`:** it now uses `Stand::progress`. With no deferrals, that counts the same members as the old rollup. The early return that `ready` no longer takes didn't change any results.
  - **`milestone_from_above`:** matches how `milestones`, `fold_top` and `climb` work, and its caller in the uncommitted `edit.rs` is consistent with it.

text:
리뷰 원문 (/code-review high --fix, 98fdf47..801fe92, src/cmd/tui.rs·src/tui/draw.rs·src/tui/mod.rs)

No correctness bugs found in the reviewed range — `--fix` had nothing to apply, the working tree is unchanged, and cargo fmt was not run. (`ReportFindings` isn't available in this session, so this reply is the report.) TUI tests pass: `cargo test --bin moai tui` → 273 passed, 0 failed, including the two new wake tests and the group-glint test.

What was verified, against the focus you gave:

- Visible spinner can't be missed. `spinner_on` reads the buffer after list/detail/form/picker/SPC-menu are drawn; the only later draws (bottom key bar) never emit SPIN glyphs. List: ratatui `List` only renders rows inside the offset window into the buffer. Detail: `Paragraph::scroll` only renders the visible slice. Idea form / picker cover the whole body (`Clear`), so hidden spinners are genuinely gone. Ask mode only covers when `back` is an Idea form — otherwise list/detail remain visible and still wake. Project layer draws static glyphs only (correctly no wake, where before it could wake for hidden in-progress issues). List title counts spin on any `work` row including scrolled-off ones, but that glyph is itself visible, so waking is correct; if a narrow window clips it off, it's neither visible nor wakes — consistent. Buffer is reset after each flush by ratatui, so no stale spinner from the previous frame.
- Glint without glyph can't happen: the glyph sits left of the title in the same row, `fit` clips from the right, and the SPC menu is right/bottom-anchored, so it can't cover a glyph without covering the title after it.
- One judgement: row glyph, count glyph, and glint all consult `App::spins`; the loop wakes from what was drawn with those answers. Removing the `!is_group` branch keeps glint aligned with the glyph.
- `spin_due`: while not spinning, every 700ms TICK wake passes `spin_due` and re-arms it without advancing; when a spinner becomes visible via a key/reload, the next step is at most one `step` away — no jump. When a spinner leaves the screen, one extra off-screen increment is possible and harmless.
- CPU: the scan is ~5k cell comparisons per frame, negligible next to drawing; wakes drop in the cases where in-progress issues exist but aren't on screen.

One trade-off, not a bug (already acknowledged in the code comment): a braille spinner character inside a visible issue title/body now causes fast wakes even with nothing in progress, where before it required an in-progress issue. Cost is capped by `SPIN_BUDGET` and ratatui's diffing sends nothing for an unchanged screen. No current issue in `.moai/issues.jsonl` contains those characters (one journal note does, but the TUI doesn't render the journal). Left as-is.

text:
/code-review high --fix 6c9b7a2 원문

I found four real issues in 6c9b7a2. I fixed two in the working tree and left two alone because they need changes outside the diff. Nothing is staged or committed. The full test suite passes (671 unit tests and 245 CLI tests). There was no ReportFindings tool in this session, so the findings are listed here only.

**Findings**
1. `src/report.rs:1494` (medium, fixed): `blocked_since` took the latest time across all the issues blocking a line. Say X has been blocked by A for ten days and is also blocked by B. If B moves today (for example todo→in_progress), X's clock resets and the ten-day `blocked_stale` warning quietly disappears. The right value is the earliest blocker time, combined with X's own `planned()` by taking whichever is later.
2. `src/report.rs:1491` (medium, fixed): when an epic or milestone is the blocker, only its members' times were counted, never the group's own `planned_at`. Scenario: epic E is deferred, so X shows under `blocked_by_deferred` and not under `blocked_stale`. `moai defer E --undo` sets only E's `planned_at`. X then shows up in `blocked_stale` right away as "N days blocked", which is the false alarm this commit set out to remove.
3. `src/report.rs:1491` (low, skipped): the same problem when the deferral is inherited. If the blocker sits under a milestone, epic or parent that was deferred and then brought back, `planned_at` changes only on that ancestor. Neither the blocker's `planned()` nor the group's `since` moves, so the stale warning fires immediately. Fixing it means walking the ancestor chain, which is well outside this hunk.
4. `src/report.rs:555` (low, skipped): the commit message says adding a member to a finished epic is handled, but that only works through `moai add`. Moving an existing old issue in with `moai edit <id> -e <epic>` doesn't update `status_since` or `planned_at`, so the epic's time stays old and the lines it blocks go stale immediately. Catching this needs a time recorded on edit, the same kind of gap the commit already accepts for `blocked_by`.

A related limit I didn't list as a bug: any column move of a blocker resets the clock, not just reopening from done. The snapshot alone can't tell the two apart.

**Changes, all in `/home/coder/workspace/moa-issue/.claude/worktrees/moai-xib6/src/report.rs`**
- **Lines 1473–1488 (doc comment on `blocked_since`):** now says it uses the earliest time across blockers, and that a group also counts its own `planned_at`, with the reasons.
- **Lines 1497–1504 (body):** a group blocker takes the later of its members' time and its own `planned_at`. The fold over blockers is now `.min()`, then combined with `i.planned()` by taking the later one:
  ```rust
  true => {
      let counted = group_since.get(x.id.as_str()).copied().unwrap_or(x.created_at.as_str());
      x.planned_at.as_deref().map_or(counted, |p| counted.max(p))
  }
  ...
  .min()
  .map_or(i.planned(), |b| b.max(i.planned()))
  ```
- **Lines 2340–2351:** two new assertions in the test `blocked_stale_counts_from_when_the_block_came_back`. One covers bringing a deferred epic back today (should not be stale). The other covers two blockers, one old and one moved today (should still be stale). Both fail on the old code.

The two skipped items still need tracker entries. I didn't create them because that would modify `.moai/`.

I reviewed `4716cf2` and found no bugs, so I changed nothing for `--fix`. The ReportFindings tool isn't available in this session, so this reply is the report.

The commit adds a `guide::handoff(id)` line (`moai note <id> "다음: <이어서 할 것>"`). The session-closing text in `CLOSING`, AGENTS.md and SKILL.md now teaches it, and the Stop hook's `closing` suggests it for each held issue. I checked the ways it could break:

- **No endless block at session close:** following the new hint doesn't release the held issue, so the Stop hook could keep firing. It won't: the hook passes when `stop_hook_active` is set and blocks only once per session (`src/cmd/hook.rs:144-145`).

- **The texts can't drift apart:** a test asserts `CLOSING.contains(&handoff("<id>"))`, and `closing_holds_on_what_is_still_held` checks that the hook prints the same line. AGENTS.md, SKILL.md and `CLOSING` match, so the existing tests that compare them still pass.
- **The design rules still hold:** `status` doesn't read the journal to show the note, and nothing new is stored in the snapshot.
- **Tests pass:** `cargo test --release` gave 670 and 245 passed, 0 failed.

The working tree has uncommitted changes in `.moai/issues.jsonl` and `.moai/journal.jsonl` only. Those are tracker data, not code, so I left them out of the review.

/code-review high --fix bfbfe5a 원문

I found one real bug in bfbfe5a and fixed it in the working tree. Nothing is staged or committed. All tests pass (673 unit, 245 CLI). I couldn't file it through ReportFindings because that tool isn't available here, so here it is:

- `src/report.rs:561` (medium) — In `group_stands_in`, `busy` counts a member as started even when its status isn't in the config. `column_of` only picks from columns in the config, so it ignores that member and falls back to `started_status`.
  - **Scenario:** default config, epic with members `qa` and `todo`, where `qa` is a leftover column or came in from a branch with an extra column. The epic reads `in_progress` with `busy = true`, so the TUI spins it and wakes every 120ms. No member under it spins, since `qa` has no spinner.
  - This breaks the rule written on `App::spins` (`src/tui/mod.rs`): if a group spins, something under it spins. Before this commit `busy` needed a member in exactly `started_status`, so this is new.

**What I changed** (only `src/report.rs`, both inside the commit's hunks):
- **Around line 561:** `busy` now counts a member only when both `cfg.knows(s)` and `cfg.is_started(s)` are true, so it uses the same columns `column_of` does. The two-column case stays false, and a comment explains why.
- **Lines ~3194–3198, in `a_group_stands_in_its_least_advanced_started_members_column`:** new assertion that members `qa` and `todo` give column `blocked` with `busy == false` under the five-column config.

**The decisions you'd already made are implemented consistently:**
- `wip`, `wip_overload`, the hook's `picks_up` and `busy` all use `Config::is_started`.
- `column_of` picks the least advanced started column in config order and falls back to `started_status`.
- Review members count as busy.
- `style::spins` still checks for `in_progress` by name, so a group in `review` doesn't spin.

`wip` and `wip_overload` still count members with statuses the config doesn't know as started. That's unchanged from before the commit and matches the `is_started` doc, so I left it.

## 리뷰 원문 — 리뷰 서브에이전트(high), main...worktree-moai-cxk8 (0347758)

I found no real bugs in commit 0347758. It does what you decided: `defer` and `defer --undo` no longer restart the stale or blocked clocks. `cargo test` passes (671 + 245 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored).

**Findings, by severity**

1. **Low, doc wording.** `src/report.rs:1485-1490` (the `blocked_since` comment) and the matching test comment at `src/report.rs:2336-2338`.
   - What's wrong: the comment says "미뤄 둔 동안에도 막힘은 이어졌고 `blocked_by_deferred` 로 드러나 있었다" and applies it to both the blocked row and its blockers. That is only true on the blocker side. When the blocked row itself is deferred, it drops out of `work` (the `out_of_plan` filter at about line 1692), so no warning shows at all while it is deferred.
   - Scenario: a row blocked for 10 days is deferred, then undone. While deferred, `status` said nothing about it. On undo it shows as "blocked_stale" at once. That outcome is correct, but the stated reason doesn't hold for this case.
   - Suggested fix: give the row's own case its real reason: "a deferred row isn't warned about, but its block didn't go away; counting the undo would turn defer→undo into a way to erase the warning". Keep the moai-2sea reason for blockers only.

2. **Low, not from this diff; noticed while checking consumers.** `src/view.rs:824`.
   - What's wrong: the warning list shows each row's age from the row's own `status_since`, not from `blocked_since`.
   - Scenario: for `blocked_stale`, a row sitting in `todo` for 30 days whose blocker came back from done 5 days ago shows "30일" under a "blocked more than 3 days" heading.
   - Suggested fix: carry the computed age in the warning, or file it as an idea. Not a regression.

**Checked and fine**

- The moai-xib6 cases still hold: a member added today to a finished epic (not stale, asserted at 2329); one old blocker plus one moved today (still stale, 2359-2364); a blocker reopened from done today (not stale, 2331-2334).
- Member undo really was a continued block: a group whose remaining unfinished members are deferred reads `done` but is Shelved and still blocks, reported as `blocked_by_deferred` (moai-0gxf). A group with every member deferred reads first column and also still blocks (moai-1c2l).
- No clock reads `planned_at` or `planned()` any more: `src/worktree.rs:177` is the overlay; `src/model.rs:219` definition; `src/guide.rs:336` overlay help; `src/cmd/defer.rs:62` only writes. Nothing in `src/tui/*`, `src/view.rs` or `src/query.rs` reads it.
- Consumers of `Stand::since`: `query::Where::since` (the `--stale` clock for groups) now moves only when a member changes column; `report::status`'s `group_since` feeds `blocked_since`; the TUI calls `group_stands` but never reads `.since`. No consumer needed the moment a group's column changed because of an undo.
- The test changes are meaningful: traced by hand, all four new `stale(...)` assertions (`back`, `mine`, `shuffled`, `undone`) would fail on the old code. Nothing xib6 tested lost coverage. `a_group_dates_its_column_from_its_members` uses no planned_at. The model.rs round-trip test checks `planned()` as a value, not a clock.
- Doc comments match the code: `Stand::since`, the rest of `blocked_since`, the note at `model.rs:155-158`.
- Code: `blocked_since` takes the earliest blocker time, then the later of that and the row's own `status_since`; with no active blocker it falls back to the row's own `status_since`. A group blocker falls back to `created_at` with no `Stand` entry, same as before.
- Other stale warnings: review-stale and wip-stale already used `status_since`, so no mixed clocks remain.

## 결정 — SPC 메뉴 하단 창 (moai-apsa)

- **자리: 몸통을 밀어 올린다(덮지 않는다).** 레이아웃에 `panel` 칸을 몸통과 키 바 사이에 두고 격자 줄 수 + 가름줄 하나만큼 잡는다. 덮으면 커서가 선 줄이 창 밑에 숨어 메뉴가 무엇에 대한 것인지를 잃는다. 목록·상세는 줄어든 높이로 `Scroll::reveal` 을 이미 부르므로 따로 굴리지 않는다. 몸통 몫은 `menu::BODY_MIN = 3`(테두리 둘 + 한 줄)을 먼저 남긴다.
- **줄 수: which-key 규칙 — 한 열을 줄 상한까지 위→아래로 채우고 다음 열.** 상한 `menu::MAX_ROWS = 8` — 격자 8 + 가름줄 + 접두어 줄 = 10줄로 사용자의 "하단 8~10칸". 오늘 뿌리는 7칸이라 **한 열 7줄**(창 전체 9줄), `SPC t`·`SPC p` 는 두세 줄로 낮게 선다. 트리가 8칸을 넘으면 열이 는다. 넓은 창에서 한 열만 서는 것이 허전하다는 말이 나오면 줄 상한을 낮추는 것이 자리다(idea 로 담음).
- **칸: `키 : 설명`.** 키는 열 안에서 오른쪽 맞춤, 열마다 제 폭(doom 의 `RET`·`SPC` 열), 열 사이 2칸. 묶음은 `+프로젝트`(옛 `프로젝트 …`), 토글은 `[켜짐]/[꺼짐]`·`[원문]/[그리기]` 를 그대로 단다 — 키만 굵고 뜻은 글자가 진다.
- **넘칠 때:** 모든 열의 설명에 같은 상한을 걸어 긴 것부터 `…` 로 자른다(한글 두 칸). 상한이 3칸(한 자 + `…`) 아래로 가야 하면 뒤 열을 빼고 접두어 줄이 `그 밖 N개 — 창을 넓히면 선다` 로 수를 댄다. 한 열도 안 들면 그 열을 폭까지 자른다.
- **접두어 줄:** 메뉴가 열린 동안 키 바 자리를 통째로 쓴다 — 왼쪽 `SPC- 메뉴` / `SPC t- 토글`(doom 의 `SPC- <leader>`), 오른쪽 끝 `Esc 닫기`·하위 층이면 `Bksp 위로`. 탐색의 키는 메뉴 안에서 안 들으므로 바를 남길 까닭이 없다. 뿌리 이름은 `menu::ROOT` 하나를 바(`SPC 메뉴`)와 함께 읽는다.
- **낮은 창:** 몸통 몫과 가름줄을 빼고 격자 줄이 0 이면(`menu::rows_for`) 격자 없이 접두어 줄 한 줄로 접는다 — `SPC-  / 검색  f 거름망 …`. 항목이 먼저고 나가는 법은 자리가 남을 때만 붙는다(Esc 는 어디서든 닫는다). 7sjm 의 낮은 창 시험 뜻(항목이 말없이 사라지지 않고 폭을 안 넘는다)은 그대로 두고 크기를 더했다.
- **차례: 표의 차례를 그대로.** doom 은 기호 → 글자 알파벳순이지만 뿌리의 차례(`/ f n r q p t` — 동작 먼저, 묶음 뒤)는 moai-hudg 에서 사람이 확정한 것이다. 정렬하면 그 결정이 말없이 뒤집힌다. 표 차례라 결정적이다.
- **순수:** 격자는 `menu::grid(&[Entry], 폭, 줄 상한) -> Grid` 가 놓고(열 우선·맞춤·자르기·뺀 수), `draw.rs` 의 `menu_panel`·`menu_line` 은 칠하기만 한다. 내용은 여전히 키 표 + `Browse::enabled` 에서만 온다.

title: SPC 메뉴 격자 줄 상한을 낮출까 — 뿌리 7칸이 넓은 창에서 왼쪽 한 열로만 서 허전하면 MAX_ROWS 를 4 안팎으로(열이 늘어 doom 화면처럼 퍼진다). 사용자의 '하단 8~10칸' 과 맞바꾸는 일이라 말이 나올 때 (moai-apsa)

## 리뷰 원문 — /code-review high --fix d01279c~1..d01279c (moai-apsa)

I found no correctness bugs in `d01279c`. The only finding was a leftover debug line in a test, which I removed. The ReportFindings tool isn't available in this session, so the finding is listed here instead.

**Finding (1)**
- `src/tui/draw.rs:3578` — low, cleanup. The new test `the_menu_panel_lines_up_and_keeps_the_cursor_in_sight_at_any_width` had a leftover `eprintln!("── {w}칸 ──\n{screen}")`. It printed the whole screen three times (at 80, 120 and 200 columns) whenever tests run with `--nocapture`. The assert messages already print the screen when a check fails, so it added nothing.

**Checked and fine**
- **Height budget:** the body always keeps at least 3 rows when the grid opens. With no room for the grid, the menu folds into the one-line prefix bar and the body gets everything.
- **`menu::grid` widths:** every line fits the width it is given. Clipping still fits when Korean characters take two columns. When only one column fits and there's no room left for text, nothing panics; `fit` trims the line. The `hidden` count is correct.
- **Shrinking body:** `Scroll` re-measures its height every frame, paging uses fixed step sizes, and nothing hit-tests clicks against the body area. While the menu is open it takes every key, so the shorter height can't leak into scrolling after it closes.
- **`fkeys`:** its old "menu is open" branch was removed, but its only caller now runs just when the menu is closed, so nothing depended on that branch.
- **Spinner check:** the panel is drawn before the buffer is scanned for spinner glyphs, and the menu no longer covers anything, so the reasoning in that comment still holds.

**Fix applied:** I deleted that one line in the worktree (`src/tui/draw.rs`). All 282 `tui::` tests passed before the change, and the 6 `the_menu` tests pass after it, with no warnings. It isn't committed. Nothing was skipped.

## 판단 — 리뷰 moai-apsa.oyz

**반영한 것**
- 새 시험에 남은 `eprintln!`(low). 받아들였다 — 80·120·200칸 그림은 단언 실패문이 이미 화면을 내므로 늘 찍을 까닭이 없다. 따로 커밋: `fix: 리뷰 moai-apsa.oyz — 메뉴 창 시험의 디버그 출력을 걷는다`.

**넘긴 것**
- 없다. 리뷰가 "봤고 문제없다" 고 한 높이 셈·폭 셈·줄어든 몸통의 스크롤·`fkeys` 가지 걷기·스피너 판정은 이쪽도 같은 판단이다 — 격자는 `rows_for` 가 몸통 몫(3)과 가름줄을 먼저 빼고 정하고, `Scroll::fit` 은 프레임마다 높이를 다시 받는다.

**리뷰 밖에서 이쪽이 정한 것 (다시 보려면)**
- 넓은 창에서 뿌리 7칸이 한 열로만 서는 것 — which-key 규칙과 "하단 8~10칸" 을 따른 결과다. 줄 상한을 낮춰 열로 퍼뜨리는 안은 idea moai-ik31 로 담았다.

text:
[리뷰 원문 — /code-review high --fix HEAD~1..HEAD]

**Finding**

- `src/hook.rs:1162` (`guard_review`), medium — **Rule 3 can tell a session to pick up a review that another worktree already has.** The commit stopped counting other worktrees' work as this session's focus, but `open` (the list of open reviews) still includes their review issues. Example: a worktree for `X` exists, `X` is in progress, and its review `X.aa` is in progress. A session in main that has picked up nothing calls `/code-review`. `focus` is now empty, so the code refuses with `open.first()`: "리뷰 이슈 X.aa 가 아직 안 집혔다 … moai mv X.aa in_progress". `X.aa` is already in progress, so doing what the message says never clears the block. If `X.aa` is still todo, the main session is sent to take over the other worktree's review. The comment in that branch ("focus 가 곧 wip") no longer holds after this change. A smaller effect of the same gap: when this session does have focus, the "열린 리뷰 줄이 있지만 … 안 매여 있다" line also listed the other worktree's reviews.

**Fix**

- I moved the "does this issue belong to another worktree" check out of `held` into a shared helper, `fn theirs(issues, away)`. It returns true when the issue, one of its ancestors, or its epic or milestone is in `away`. `held` uses it as before.
- `guard_review` now leaves those reviews out of `open`, so its refusal message and the stray-review list measure the same way as `held`.
- New unit test: `a_review_another_worktree_holds_is_not_named_here`.

**Looked at and left alone**

- When everything picked up belongs to other worktrees, Rule 2 now blocks edits in main. The commit's own test asserts this, so it's intended.
- `guard_close` no longer asks for `-m` when main closes a review that belongs to another worktree. This follows from the same rule that work there isn't this session's focus, so I left it.
- A single tool call still runs `report::wip` several times, and runs git twice whenever something is picked up, which is normal inside a worktree. That's slower, not wrong, and the commit acknowledges the cost.
- `names` also adds non-id names, such as the main branch name or a detached HEAD hash. They only drop something if they exactly match an issue id, so they're harmless.

[판단] 반영: guard_review 가 옆 워크트리의 리뷰를 열린 리뷰로 세던 것 — theirs 로 held 와 같은 자를 쓰게 고침(28c046c). 그대로 둠: 옆 일이 전부면 main 에서 규칙 2 가 서는 것(의도, 시험이 단언), 옆 리뷰를 main 이 닫을 때 -m 을 안 요구하는 것(같은 규칙의 귀결), 이름 후보에 id 아닌 이름이 섞이는 것(정확히 id 와 같을 때만 뺀다). 넘김: 도구 호출당 wip 여러 번·워크트리 목록 두 번 읽는 값 → moai-9cjg. 이름이 id 가 아닌 워크트리에서 집은 일 → moai-f69b.

note: 원문·판단을 붙였다. 옆 리뷰를 규칙 3 이 대던 것 반영(28c046c), 값은 moai-9cjg·이름 한계는 moai-f69b 로 넘김
main 에 병합 — 옆 워크트리 이름이 가리키는 일과 그 밑을 훅 초점에서 뺀다. 리뷰 moai-asjt.51b 반영

title: status 의 blocked_by_deferred 목록이 줄마다 칸 나이를 대 '미룬 것에 N일 막힘' 으로 읽힌다 — 날짜로 안 거는 경고에 나이 열을 낼지 정한다

text:
## 리뷰 원문 — 리뷰 서브에이전트(high), main...worktree-moai-7azq (d0207a0)

Review of commit d0207a0 (`ages` on `Warning`): nothing blocking. The ages are measured the same way the warnings are judged. There is one real gap in test coverage and one minor mismatch with duplicate ids. `cargo test` passes (672 unit, 245 CLI).

**Findings, by severity**

1. **Medium: no test covers the bug that was actually fixed.** Test at src/report.rs:2402, view change at src/view.rs:824-830.
   - `a_warning_carries_the_age_it_was_judged_by` only checks that `report::status` fills `ages`. The bug was in `view::preview`, which ignored the judged age and re-measured from `status_since`.
   - Failure scenario: someone reverts the view.rs hunk to `days_since(&i.status_since, now)`, or refactors `preview` and drops the `w.ages.get(id)` lookup. Every test still passes and "30일" comes back under "3일 넘게 막힘".
   - The report test also can't show it would have failed before the change: the old code has no `ages` field, so it wouldn't compile.
   - Fix: view.rs tests already have `issue()`, `cfg()` and `plain()` (around src/view.rs:1480-1510). Add a test that builds the blocker scenario, calls `crate::report::status(...)` and then `view::status(&st, &issues, &cfg, now, at, &Origin::default(), 0)`. Assert the `argos-0002` row contains "5일" and not "30일".

2. **Low: duplicate ids can show the age of one line next to a different line.** src/report.rs:1593 (`or_insert`) against src/view.rs:654.
   - `rows` (`rotting` / `stuck` / `forgotten`) are filtered from `work` and keep file order, so `or_insert` keeps the first qualifying line in the file.
   - `view::status` builds `by_id` with `.collect()`, where the last line in the file wins. `preview` takes priority, glyph and title from that line.
   - Scenario: line 1 is `argos-0005` in review, 10 days old; line 2 is also `argos-0005`, in review, 4 days old. Both qualify for `stale_review`. The row shows line 2 (4 days) with "10일".
   - If only one twin qualifies, the age is correct. Glyph and title still come from the last line, but that was already true before this commit.
   - Fix: use `self.ages.insert(i.id.clone(), d)`, so the last qualifying line wins like `by_id`. `duplicate_id` already flags the data, so this is cosmetic.

3. **Informational, nothing to change: other day-less warnings still print column age.**
   - `no_epic`, `no_milestone` and `blocked_by_deferred` fall back to `status_since` age in `preview`. They aren't judged by days, so "N일 in column" is neutral context, not a contradiction of a threshold.
   - `blocked_by_deferred` could be read as "blocked for N days" while the number is column age. That predates this commit; say if you want it tracked.

**Checked and fine**
- Same timestamp as the filter: stale_review/stale_progress use `days_since(&i.status_since, now)` in both filter and ages; blocked_stale calls `blocked_since` with the same arguments and `now`. `days_since` is `div_euclid(86400)`, thresholds use `>`, no off-by-one; `ages.len() == ids.len()` holds.
- Lifetimes fit; `BTreeMap` already imported; JSON key order deterministic; `skip_serializing_if` works.
- Nothing rewrites `w.ids` after `status()`.
- Other surfaces: TUI only counts warnings; hook sums `count`; multi-project overview shows counts; `preview` has one caller. Nothing else re-measures warning ages.

text:
## 리뷰 원문 — /code-review high --fix, worktree-moai-2v3w (b754b39)

I found one real bug in the diff and fixed it; the fix is in the working tree and not committed. The full test suite passes (`cargo test --release`: 672 unit tests and 245 CLI tests).

**Finding**

- `src/store.rs:254` (severity: medium) — The unreadable-line tally is one global for the whole process, but `moai tui` writes to several projects in one process (each project on its layer is a separate `Repo`, written through `App::write` → `repo.with_write`). This goes wrong in two ways:
  1. **Silent about a damaged file:** browse project A, which has 3 unreadable lines, without changing it, then write to project B, which is clean. B's write resets `seen` to 0, so on exit nothing is printed and A's damage is never mentioned.
  2. **Wrong project named:** write to A while carrying 2 unreadable lines, then work in B. On exit the warning says it "kept 2 unreadable lines" and points to `moai show`. That runs against the current directory (B, or no repo at all), so it shows the wrong lines or tells you to run `init`.

**What I changed**

- `src/store.rs`: `TALLY` is now `Mutex<Vec<(PathBuf, Tally)>>`, one entry per repo root in the order they were first written. `with_write` updates the entry for `self.root`, and `unreadable_tally()` is replaced by `unreadable_tallies()`. The `Tally::after` function and its unit test are unchanged.
- `src/main.rs`: `carried()` prints one warning line per project. When a project isn't the repo for the current directory, the suggested command is `moai -C <root> show`. Plain CLI runs (including `-C`) still say `moai show`, because the directory change happens before the lookup. It returns early when every tally is clean, so the normal path doesn't pay for `Repo::find`.

**Checked and left alone:**
- The tally is recorded before the journal append, so a journal error still counts the snapshot write. That's correct, because the write did happen.
- A write that returns early on a validation error records nothing. That matches the old behaviour, and the TUI already shows the error.
- If a session carried lines earlier and more lines broke later, the "carried" message wins and doesn't mention the newer count. This only happens when another process damages the file mid-session, so I didn't treat it as a bug.

## 판단

**반영** (worktree-moai-2v3w 의 e25ccb9)
- 1(중) 셈이 프로세스에 하나라 탐색기가 여러 프로젝트에 쓰면 A 의 상한 줄을 B 의 깨끗한 쓰기가 덮고, A 에서 들고 간 줄을 엉뚱한 저장소의 `moai show` 로 가리킨다 — 받았다. tui/layer.rs:445 `enter_project` 가 `App.repo` 를 갈아 끼우는 것을 확인했다. 리뷰가 고친 그대로(뿌리마다 Tally, 부른 자리가 아니면 `moai -C <뿌리> show`) 커밋했고 cargo test 672+245 통과.

**반영하지 않은 것과 까닭**
- 리뷰가 "확인하고 둔" 셋(저널 실패 전에 센다·검증 실패는 안 센다·들고 간 뒤 새로 상한 수는 carried 말이 이긴다)은 그대로 둔다. 셋째는 세션 중 다른 프로세스가 파일을 상하게 할 때만 나고, 들고 간 말 자체는 참이다.
- `moai -C <뿌리> show` 의 경로를 셸 따옴표로 감싸지 않는다 — 안내 문구이고 공백 든 뿌리는 드물다. 넘기지 않는다.

**넘긴 것 (이슈 번호와 함께)**
- 없음.

title: 시각이 지금보다 뒤면 경고 목록이 '-1일' 을 낸다 — days_since 가 div_euclid 로 음수를 돌린다

text:
## 리뷰 원문 — 리뷰 서브에이전트(high), main...worktree-moai-hcx3 (b947b7a)

I found no real bugs in b947b7a (`cargo test`: 686 + 246 pass). There are two design questions, two test gaps and a small efficiency point. Nothing in `holding` can lose the age.

**Medium: the age can be older than the blocked row's own story.** src/report.rs:1876-1886
- This is what you asked for, taken literally. But unlike `blocked_since` (report.rs:1533), the deferral age is never capped by any time on the blocked row or the blocker. So the "when the plan contradiction began" reading can overshoot.
- Scenario 1: blocker B was deferred 40 days ago. Row H is created today with `blocked_by = [B]`, and `moai status` lists H as "40일". The same happens if H itself was undeferred yesterday: its own deferral kept it out of the plan until then.
- Scenario 2: epic E was deferred 20 days ago. Issue B was reopened from done yesterday, or moved into E with `edit -e` yesterday. `deferred_sources[B]` includes E (`closed_by_hand` only drops done rows), so the list shows 20 days although the contradiction is one day old.
- Suggested fix: cap it like `blocked_since`, using `max(earliest deferral, i.status_since)`. That fixes scenario 1 and keeps both "N days blocked" clocks on the same rule. Scenario 2 can't be fixed exactly because membership-move time isn't stored (moai-bbzg); capping with the blocker's `status_since` would cover the reopen case.
- If you keep the literal rule, say "can be older than the row" in the comment block at report.rs:1868-1871.

**Answers to your two questions:**
- Undefer, then defer again: `cmd/defer.rs:59` clears `deferred_at` on `--undo` and sets a fresh time on the next defer, so it shows 2 days, not 30. The first stretch leaves no trace in the snapshot. That's correct: the contradiction really paused.
- Member deferred 40 days ago, inside an epic deferred 20 days ago: `Shelf::every` returns both, so the min is 40. That's correct. No test covers this case.

**Low: tests don't cover the group or multi-source paths.**
- Both new tests fail on the old code (report test gets `None`, view test falls back to "30일").
- The third case in the report test (`older` deferred 09-01) gives 30, which equals the column age from `make`. An implementation that used column age would pass that assertion; move `older` to e.g. 09-05.
- Missing cases: a blocker whose own deferral is older than its epic's; a group blocker that itself is deferred; a group reading done with Shelved `aside` members, so the age comes from the aside members, not the group id.

**Low: duplicate work, paid only when `waiting` is non-empty.** report.rs:1875
- `deferred_sources(issues)` rebuilds `groups`, `milestones`, `deferred_roots_in` (including `members_in` and `counted` per deferred group) and a second `Shelf`. `status` already has `group`, `mile_of` and `roots`.
- `holding` also runs twice per waiting row (`by_deferred`, then `shelved_since`).
- Suggested fix: a `deferred_sources_in(all, &epic_of, &mile_of, &roots)` variant that `deferred_sources` wraps. `held()` (report.rs:1398) would benefit too. The results are identical either way.

**Nit:** src/model.rs:614. If `deferred_at` is ahead of `now` (another machine's clock via `--worktree`, or `MOAI_NOW` set earlier), `div_euclid` gives -1 and the list shows "-1일". Not new (`status_since` has the same exposure), but this commit gives it one more timestamp.

**Checked and fine:**
- Every `Blocker::Deferred` path has an entry in `sources`, and `sources` has the same keys as `status`'s `roots`: plain deferred issue; issue under a deferred epic/milestone/parent; group deferred and not reading done (including `Waiting::Nothing`); group reading done with Shelved `aside` (aside members each in roots for a reason other than the group's own deferral); empty group only reaches Deferred if itself out of plan.
- `.unwrap_or("")` is effectively unreachable: every source comes from `Shelf::own`, which requires `is_put_off`, so `deferred_at` is always `Some`.
- `deferred_sources` and `status` agree (same maps, same `deferred_roots_in`, same short-circuit; `by_id` last-wins everywhere).
- Duplicate ids: `ages` inserts per row, last qualifying row wins.
- `--worktree`: `overlay` swaps whole rows; one consistent snapshot.
- Undefer: `--undo` clears `deferred_at`, so a stale time can't keep aging a row back in plan.
- Doc comments match the code; `view::preview` reads `w.ages` first.
- Project rules: `report` stays pure, `view` only renders, nothing derived stored.
moai-8tav 를 이어받아 집는다 (2026-09-14, 사용자 요청). 5e7w 쪽 moai-aucs 는 옆 세션이 중복으로 지웠다(6db4a7a) — cl8h 몫은 moai-k9yb 로 따로 남는다.

## 판단

**반영** (worktree-moai-hcx3 의 fix 커밋)
- 중: 나이가 막힌 줄·막는 줄의 이야기보다 이를 수 있다 — 받았다. 미룬 날과 `blocked_since`(막음이 선 날) 중 늦은 것으로 잰다. 40일 전에 미룬 줄에 오늘 막힌 줄은 0일, 막는 줄이 어제 done 에서 되돌아 나왔으면 1일. blocked_stale 과 같은 자라 두 "막힌 날수" 가 한 규칙으로 선다. 사용자와 정한 "모순이 선 때" 의 뜻 안이다. 소속을 옮긴 시각은 여전히 못 잰다(moai-bbzg 와 같은 한계).
- 하(시험): 묶음 제 미룸, 끝난 것으로 읽는 묶음이 기다리는 미룬 멤버, 한 막는 줄의 미룸 둘(제 40일·에픽 20일), 막음이 늦게 선 두 경우를 더했다. 칸 나이 30일과 같던 `older` 단언은 26일로 옮겼다.
- 하(효율): `deferred_sources_in` 을 두고 status 가 이미 가진 group·mile_of·roots 로 부른다. `deferred_sources` 는 그것을 감싼다.

**반영하지 않은 것과 까닭**
- `holding` 을 줄마다 두 번 부르는 것 — 경고가 설 때만, 미룬 것에 막힌 줄 수만큼이라 값이 작다. 한 번으로 줄이려면 by_deferred 필터가 결과를 들고 다녀야 해 코드가 갈라진다. 그대로 둔다.
- `held()` 도 `deferred_sources_in` 로 옮기는 것 — 이 변경 밖이다. 결과는 같다.

**넘긴 것 (이슈 번호와 함께)**
- nit: 시각이 now 보다 뒤면 '-1일' (days_since 음수, 이 변경 전부터) — idea moai-xat0.

## 리뷰 원문 — /code-review high --fix, worktree-moai-0cl3 (1ea6501)

I found no bugs in `worktree-moai-0cl3` (commit `1ea6501`), so `--fix` had nothing to change and the working tree is untouched.

**What I checked:**
- **Call sites:** all six places that put a path into a suggested command now pass the raw path to `shell_word`. They are in `src/cmd/project.rs` (add and color), `src/view.rs` (`shell_arg`), `src/tui/draw.rs` (`place_about`) and `src/cmd/skill.rs`. The display lines still use `one_line`, which is right. `shown` in `project::add` is still used for its first line, so nothing is left unused.
- **Removing `one_line` loses no protection:** `sanitize` only strips control characters, and the new `$'…'` branch escapes every control character. Nothing that used to be cleaned now reaches the terminal raw.
- **The `$'…'` escaping:** `\\`, `\'`, `\n`, `\t` and per-byte `\xHH` are all valid in bash and zsh. Every byte is written as exactly two hex digits, so a following letter can't be read as part of the escape. Multi-byte C1 characters come out as their UTF-8 bytes.
- **Folding `skill.rs` into the shared function:** the old copy left all non-ASCII characters unquoted, so something like a non-breaking space went through bare. The shared version quotes anything that isn't a letter or digit, which is stricter, and `=` is still accepted.
- **Build and tests:** the release build has no warnings. Both `shell_word` unit tests pass, including the one that runs the output through bash, and so does `a_hint_spells_a_path_with_a_tab_so_the_shell_gets_that_directory`.

**Two things to be aware of, neither a bug in this diff:**
- **`-` quoting doesn't work, and this predates the diff.** The comment on `shell_word` in `src/text.rs` says it wraps paths starting with `-` so clap won't read them as flags. Quotes don't do that: the shell removes `'-rf'`'s quotes before clap sees it, so it's still a flag. The real fix is a `./` prefix or a `--` separator. It rarely matters because these paths are almost always absolute. It isn't recorded yet; `moai idea add` would capture it.
- **`$'…'` only works in bash and zsh (and newer POSIX shells).** fish and older dash won't unquote it. Before this change the command pointed at the wrong directory in every shell, so this is still an improvement.

text:
리뷰 원문 — /code-review high --fix HEAD~1..HEAD (fa36d3b, src/skill.rs)

**Finding**

- `src/skill.rs:656` (medium): when `MOAI_BLESS=1` and `marketplace.json` isn't valid JSON, the text fallback grabs the first `"name": "` anywhere in the file. If the top-level `name` line is missing (say a merge conflict hunk dropped it), that first match is `owner.name` = `"moai"`. Bless would then quietly rename the marketplace to `moai` and write the whole plugin tree with that name.
  - The code comment claims a wrong value would be caught by the comparison that follows. That's false: with bless on, the files are written from those values first and then compared against themselves, so the check always passes.

**Fix (in the working tree, not committed)**
